authoredPrompt: This figure is a single sketch on an unlabeled coordinate plane showing a position vector broken into its horizontal and vertical parts. Two thin axes with arrowheads at all four ends meet at the origin; neither axis carries a name or numbers, though a few short tick marks are spaced along them. An orange arrow runs from the origin up and to the right into the first quadrant and is labeled v = ai + bj, with v, i, and j set in bold. A dark blue arrow extends from the origin along the horizontal axis to the point lying directly beneath the orange arrow's tip and is labeled ai below the axis. A second dark blue arrow rises vertically from that point to the tip of the orange arrow and is labeled bj. The two blue arrows and the orange one enclose a right triangle whose legs are the components and whose hypotenuse is the vector. Drawing the components as arrows joined head to tail makes the vector read as their sum rather than as an abstract pair. The sketch supports the magnitude of v being sqrt(a^2 + b^2), read straight off the legs of the triangle.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for a: the learner changes the horizontal component, the ai arrow length and the endpoint of v move left or right, and the horizontal part of ai + bj is separated from the vertical part.
- Slider for b: the learner changes the vertical component, the bj arrow height and the endpoint of v move up or down, and the vertical part of the vector sum becomes visible.
- Toggle between components and magnitude triangle: the learner switches from labeled component arrows to a right-triangle view with side lengths and sqrt(a^2 + b^2), showing why the vector magnitude follows the Pythagorean theorem.
authoredContext:
The magnitude of v = ai + bj is given as | v |= a 2 + b 2. See the figure.

Plot showing vectors in rectangular coordinates in terms of i and j. The position vector v (in orange) extends from the origin to some point (a,b) in Q1. The horizontal (ai) and vertical (bj) components are shown.
sourceQmd: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 8: Further Applications of Trigonometry

discrepancies: The horizontal component is labeled just 'i' and the vertical component just 'j', whereas the source labels them 'ai' and 'bj' (with the scalar coefficients a and b explicitly shown).

The vector equation annotation 'v = ai + bj' that sits alongside the orange vector in the source is not rendered correctly; in the screenshot only a stray italic 'j' appears near the midpoint of the orange vector.
The generated axes carry a full set of numeric-position tick marks on both axes, while the source shows only a couple of sparse ticks, making the plane look more gridded than the original.
The blue used for the component vectors is a very dark navy (#16365c) versus the medium blue of the source, a minor color shift.
evaluation.notes: The vector-decomposition topology (orange resultant plus head-to-tail blue horizontal and vertical components with arrowheads on a double-arrowed axis) is faithfully reproduced and the a/b sliders, magnitude-triangle toggle, and 4-step player are genuinely functional, but the default-state labels are wrong: components read 'i'/'j' instead of 'ai'/'bj' and the 'v = ai + bj' equation annotation collapses to a stray 'j', so the figure no longer reads as a drop-in replacement for the source.
action_items: Fix the multi-tspan equation label so the full bold-italic string 'v = ai + bj' renders beside the orange vector; currently only the final 'j' tspan is visible (likely an anchor/move interaction bug in addLabel).

Restore the scalar coefficients in the component labels: render 'ai' (italic a + bold i) under the horizontal arrow and 'bj' (italic b + bold j) beside the vertical arrow, matching the source exactly.
Reduce the axis tick set to match the source's sparse ticks (or remove numeric ticks) so the default composition matches the textbook figure.
Lighten the component-vector blue toward the source's medium blue for closer color fidelity.
